rows.name: Clear goal and feedback
rows.note: “King · slain100%” contradicted two King death screens and a still-unreachedD34 goal; I could proceed, but milestones and locked-bank wording needed interpretation.

rows.name: Interesting decisions
rows.note: The Mother patch choice traded “12/12” safe returns against “83→17%” boss reach, while my9/12 scroll patch preserved the attempt; lapse: several purchase and forecast changes grouped their effects, obscuring which edit caused the delta.

rows.name: Mastery curve
rows.note: “D33 13→63%” with D34still“<13%” taught me to separate reaching the King from defeating him and combine two mirror counters; lapse: I could not resolve his low-health cadence cutoff into a winning setup during this horizon.

rows.name: Tension, risk and release
rows.note: Petra survived gas at “3/18hp” and secured “$584” through my emergency scroll rule; lapse: early familiar floors became highly safe Swift sections with little uncertainty before the next wall.

rows.name: Feel and juice
rows.note: Visible sword arcs, spark hits and “BLOCKED” amplified fights, and gear/rule controls responded; routine targeting was sometimes crowded and did not invite interaction for its own pleasure. Audio unassessed: no listening evidence.

rows.name: Surprise and variety
rows.note: “boss → read silence” changed how I handled Queen summons after gas, stunlock and reflective wardens had demanded different responses; lapse: repeated Queen wave clearing became familiar in consecutive normal watches.

rows.name: Expression and identity
rows.note: My five custom rules included “depth≥28→read silence” and “hp<30%→read recall” rather than an untouched default, backed by two mirror packages; lapse: many redundant locked package rows swamped the small authored part of the editor.

rows.name: Story to tell
rows.note: Petra at the Mother went from no heals and gas to “read unknown,” an enchant and a recall that saved the carry; lapse: bulk absence summaries reduced some later runs to totals rather than preserving their turns. Same-day recollection only; delayed recall remains pending.

rows.name: Flow and pacing
rows.note: In-run: normal combats gave changing tactical traces, with automatic quiet4x and Swift familiar floors, but D28“Live” once held an unchanged trace until pause/resume. Check-in: read/report decisions fit the5/20minute returns but long editors and modal purchasing added friction. Cadence:20m brought a record,4h a death/workforce spend,8h deeper failures/training; tool-buffer and infrastructure waits excluded.

rows.name: Fairness and legibility of failure
rows.note: Rook at “16/54hp” had “second wind·no use,” “drink heal·no item,” and “bank at44%·going home” before the fatal18hit; cheap next heirs kept retries available. Lapse: the final King screen offered five fixes but “none beats1/12 as is,” giving weak help for my next revision.

rows.name: Autonomy and exploration
rows.note: I kept “GUARD32HP” Drul over a new “SCOUT24HP” and chose rescue/recall experiments or ignored the offered Lich trial; the main route remained a mostly linear descent and package ordering was constrained.

rows.name: Collection and progression
rows.note: Within runs I gained carry, depths and “axe+13”; across runs FighterL7, six custom slots and learned vocabulary persisted; Scout, Quartermaster, Apprentice and “Drillmaster+9levels” removed chores. Lapse: queued forge spending of“$9000” outweighed one absence’s earnings without a clear advance budget estimate I could retain.

rows.name: Atmosphere and audiovisual appeal
rows.note: Torchlit crypts, red Foundry and grey Sanctum plus framed town/rule art stayed coherent throughout. Lapse: phone headers truncated“unbow…” and overlapping combat sprites sometimes hid individual actors. Visual atmosphere assessed; sound unassessed.

rows.name: Return payoff (idle)
rows.note: “1run” to a D31 record after20m, two runs with a Queen death after4h, then “4runs·+$13121” and King failures after8h each prompted different configuration choices. Lapse: I could not predict the scale of net returns before leaving, especially after worker expenditures.

rows.name: Attribution of the agent's play (idle)
rows.note: My reserved“depth≥28→read silence” erased Queen summons, while my “depth≥33→second wind” fired on a warden before the King and then showed“no use.” Lapse: the decisive low-health King turns fell through to package defaults whose priority I could not freely reorder.
